title: Which horror villain is waiting at the end of the hallway
dek: The light is on, the door is open and the house is making a noise it should not. Twelve questions about fear, costumes and 3am.

questions.prompt: The house makes a noise at 3am. Not a creak. A drawer.

options.label: Go and look. Torch, no shoes
Wake someone and make them look with you
Stay still and listen properly
Text the group: anyone awake?

questions.prompt: Pick the hallway you'd walk down.
questions.helper: There's a light on at the far end.

options.label: Hospital green, one door ajar
options.alt: An empty hospital corridor under strip lights

options.label: Hotel carpet, endless identical doors
options.alt: A long hotel corridor lit by tall windows

options.label: Cellar stairs, switch at the bottom
options.alt: Brick steps leading down to a dark cellar door

options.label: A forest path swallowed by fog
options.alt: A path through a beech forest in thick fog

questions.prompt: A door that shouldn't be open:

options.label: Close it and never mention it
Look inside, just once

questions.prompt: Fear is something you can enjoy from a safe distance.
I laugh at exactly the wrong moment.
Someone in the group is lying and everyone is being polite about it.

options.label: You already know. Say nothing
Ask a question that catches them
Watch how they treat the quiet one
Make it a game and see who cracks

questions.prompt: A costume tells you more than a conversation.
You're hosting. Nobody's talking. The clock is very loud.

options.label: Tell the worst story you know
Ask one question and let them fill it
Put music on and disappear for a bit
Make sure everyone has a drink

questions.prompt: I notice the exits when I walk into a room.
A stranger at the bus stop says, 'You look like someone I used to know.'

options.label: Ask who
Say 'people say that' and move seats
Give them a completely fake name
Smile and say nothing

questions.prompt: I'd rather be feared than forgotten.
The light in your room flickers. Three times. Then stops.

options.label: Ignore it. Old wiring
Film it for the group chat
Change the bulb properly
Leave it off and sit in the dark

results.name: Ghostface
results.blurb: You turn a quiet night into a bit. You understand horror as a language — the timing, the fake-out, the joke that lands right before the scare. Under the performance you're unusually good at reading what people are afraid of, which is exactly why you should be careful with it.
strengths: Reads the room like a script
Makes fear fun instead of heavy
Knows when to drop the bit
results.watchOut: The joke that lands hardest can also cut deepest. Check first.

results.name: Michael Myers
results.blurb: You don't rush and you don't explain. You decide something once and then keep going, at the same pace, until it's finished. People find the silence unnerving, but it isn't emptiness — it's a very long attention span pointed at one thing.
results.watchOut: Silence reads as absence. Tell one person what you're actually thinking.

results.name: Pennywise
results.blurb: You know the fastest way into a room is a laugh. You say the outrageous thing, get everyone looking, and somehow make it work. You're brilliant at finding the exact fear or desire that motivates a person — use that on a stage, not on your friends.
strengths: Finds the joke inside a bad night
results.watchOut: Attention is not the same as connection. Let someone else have the punchline.

results.name: Carrie White
results.tagline: Quiet, watchful, one bad day from legend
results.blurb: You notice everything and say almost none of it. You've been underestimated enough that you've built a whole interior life nobody at the table knows about. When it finally matters you're capable of far more than anyone prepared for — a gift or a warning, depending on the week.
strengths: Deeply loyal to the few who are kind
results.watchOut: Say the thing before it becomes the whole story. You're allowed to be angry out loud.

results.name: Count Dracula
results.tagline: Charming, patient, always the guest who stays
results.blurb: You have excellent manners and a very long memory. Charm opens more doors than force and you're happy to wait for the right moment. People invite you in because you're interesting, and they're usually right to — although they rarely read the whole invitation.
strengths: Reads a situation before entering it
Unhurried in a way people find magnetic
results.watchOut: You don't need to be invited everywhere. Some doors can stay closed.

results.name: Leatherface
results.tagline: Does the work, hates the fuss
results.blurb: You are far more competent than you let on and deeply uninterested in being perceived. You handle the unpleasant job while everyone else argues about it. There's a real tenderness under the blunt exterior — you just express it by making sure nobody has to deal with the mess.
strengths: Does the thing nobody wants to do
results.watchOut: Being useful isn't a personality. Let someone see the soft part on purpose.

results.name: Freddy Krueger
results.tagline: Turns your own head against you
results.blurb: You know exactly which question will keep someone awake. That's not cruelty by default — it's pattern recognition with a mischievous streak. You're at your best when you use it to puncture pomposity, and at your worst when you use it because you're bored.
strengths: Never lets a silence get comfortable
results.watchOut: Being right about someone's fear isn't permission to use it. Put it down.

results.name: The Babadook
results.tagline: The thing you keep in the basement
results.blurb: There's something you've decided not to look at. It's not monstrous — it's grief, or anger, or the version of events you'd rather not narrate. You've built routines around it. It keeps getting bigger in the dark, and quieter when somebody finally asks.
strengths: Protective of the people in your care
Honest once you decide to be
results.watchOut: The basement is not a solution. Say the thing to someone safe.
